questions.question:
Choose the option which is similar in meaning to the underlined word.

Pushkin, the great Russian poet was a **__remarkable __**man.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Astounding**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"remarkable"** means something extraordinary or worthy of attention; it refers to something that stands out because it is unusual or impressive. (असाधारण)

 
 
• **Example:** The scientist’s remarkable discovery changed the course of history.
 

 
• **"Astounding"** also means something incredibly surprising or amazing. It conveys a similar meaning to "remarkable," as both refer to something extraordinary or beyond ordinary expectations. (चकित कर देने वाला)

 
 
• **Example:** The magician's astounding performance left the audience speechless.
 

 
• Hence, the word **"Astounding"** is the closest in meaning to **"Remarkable."**

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Astounding**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Normal** (सामान्य): Something that is usual or typical, without anything extraordinary.
 
 
• **Example:** It is normal to feel nervous before an important exam.
 
 
 
 
• **Insignificant** (महत्वहीन): Something that is not important or lacks any notable value.
 
 
• **Example:** The error was so insignificant that nobody noticed it.
 
 
 
 
• **Typical** (सामान्य/प्रचलित): Representing what is usual or expected for a particular thing.
 
 
• **Example:** It was a typical summer day, sunny and warm.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect sentence.

options.text: Every piece sold here is well-designed and crafted to retain its originality.
Folktales are a kind of stories that get passed on from generation to generation.
The Nilgiris are the most productive mountains at the south and is too famous.
There are not many followers of Gandhiji these days.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**To answer this question, let's analyze each sentence to identify the grammatically and contextually incorrect one:**

__
 
• **1) Every piece sold here is well-designed and crafted to retain its originality.**
 
 
• This sentence describes the quality of items being sold.
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 
 
• **2) Folktales are a kind of stories that get passed on from generation to generation.**
 __
 
• This sentence talks about folktales and their transmission over generations.
 
• This sentence is erroneous__ because "a kind of stories" is incorrect. The correct phrase should be "a kind of story" (singular to agree with "a kind").
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "Folktales are a kind of story that gets passed on from generation to generation."
 
 
 
• **3) The Nilgiris are the most productive mountains at the south and is too famous.**
 __
 
• This sentence discusses the Nilgiris mountains.
 
• The sentence is erroneous__ because it contains subject-verb agreement and context issues:
 __
 
• "The Nilgiris" is plural, so the verb "is" should be replaced with "are."
 
• "At the south" should be replaced with "in the south" for correct prepositional usage.
 
• "Too famous" is awkward and should be replaced with "very famous."
 
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "The Nilgiris are the most productive mountains in the south and are very famous."
 
 
 
• **4) There are not many followers of Gandhiji these days.**
 
 
• This sentence refers to the decline in followers of Gandhiji.
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• Correcting subject-verb agreement errors is crucial to ensure grammatical accuracy.__
 
• __Using appropriate prepositions and avoiding awkward phrases helps improve contextual clarity.__

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__ 
 
• The preposition "**on**" is commonly used with verbs like "elaborate" to indicate the subject or topic being discussed. 
 
• In the given sentence, the scientist is explaining or expanding "**on**" the implications of the experiment, which makes "on" the correct preposition. 
 
• **Options 1, 3**, and 4 are incorrect because they do not fit the context of elaborating on a specific topic. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**. 
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The scientist elaborated **on**__ the implications of the experiment during his lecture."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
 
 
• **Option 1: "over"** is incorrect because it does not convey the idea of explaining or expanding on a topic. 
 
• **Option 3: "with"** is incorrect because it implies association rather than elaboration on a topic. 
 
• **Option 4: "for"** is incorrect because it suggests purpose or benefit rather than the act of elaboration. 
</ul

questions.question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

The doctor said, "Your father is going to recover within the next two days."

options.text: The doctor said that his father was going to recover within the following two days.
The doctor said that his father is going to recover within the following two days.
The doctor said that his father is going to recover within the next two days.
The doctor said that his father was going to recover within the previous two days.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The doctor said that his father was going to recover within the following two days.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Direct to Indirect Speech:**
 
 
• The reporting verb "said" remains unchanged as it is a statement.
 
• The present continuous tense "is going" is converted to the past continuous tense "was going" to maintain the sequence of tenses.
 
• The time expression "next two days" is changed to "following two days" as per the rules of indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun Changes:**
 
 
• The pronoun "your" is changed to "his" to reflect the perspective of the reported speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Quotation marks are removed in indirect speech.
 
• The sentence is restructured to follow the rules of indirect narration.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *The doctor said that his father was going to recover within the following two days.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** The doctor said that his father is going to recover within the following two days.
 
 
• Incorrect because the present continuous "is going" is not changed to the past continuous "was going," violating the rules of indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** The doctor said that his father is going to recover within the next two days.
 
 
• Incorrect because the present continuous tense "is going" is not converted to the past continuous, and "next two days" is not converted to "following two days."
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** The doctor said that his father was going to recover within the previous two days.
 
 
• Incorrect because "previous two days" changes the time reference and alters the meaning of the statement.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

He told her that the documents had already been signed before she had called.

options.text: He said, "The documents were already signed before you called."
He said to her, "The documents have already been signed before you had called."
He said to her, "The documents had already been signed before you called."
He told her, "The documents have already been signed before you have called."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He told her that the documents had already been signed before she had called.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• The reporting verb "told" remains in the past tense, maintaining the narrative flow.
 
 
 
• **Tense Conversion:**
 
 
• In indirect speech, "had already been signed" is in past perfect tense, which remains unchanged in direct speech as "had already been signed."
 
• "She had called" changes to "you called," converting the indirect reference to a direct one.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun Changes:**
 
 
• "Her" changes to "you" to match the direct speech perspective.
 
• The sentence structure aligns with the conversation between "he" and "her."
 
 
 
• **Punctuation:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a period.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He said to her, ‘The documents had already been signed before you called.’"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "He said, ‘The documents were already signed before you called.’"
 
 
• The tense "were already signed" is incorrect as it changes the meaning from past perfect to past simple.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "He said to her, ‘The documents have already been signed before you had called.’"
 
 
• The use of "have already been signed" in present perfect tense is incorrect for a past action.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He told her, ‘The documents have already been signed before you have called.’"
 
 
• The tense "have already been signed" and "have called" are incorrect for the context.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

Her family will have accepted her decision by next year.

options.text: Her decision will be accepted by her family by next year.
Her decision will be being accepted by her family by next year.
Her decision will have been accepted by her family by next year.
Her decision will have being accepted by her family by next year.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Her family will have accepted her decision by next year."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "her decision" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "will have accepted" to "will have been accepted" (future perfect passive).
 
• Keep the phrase "by her family" to indicate the original subject performing the action.
 
• Ensure the time phrase "by next year" remains at the end of the sentence for proper context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"Her decision will have been accepted by her family by next year."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Her decision will be accepted by her family by next year." – Incorrect tense (future simple passive).
 
• **Option 2:** "Her decision will be being accepted by her family by next year." – Incorrect tense (future continuous passive).
 
• **Option 4:** "Her decision will have being accepted by her family by next year." – Incorrect grammar (misuse of "being").
</ul

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the primary advantage of skill-based education over traditional pedagogy?

options.text: It reduces the duration of education
It eliminates the need for academic knowledge
It bridges the gap between learning and employability
It focuses solely on manual skills

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 3: It bridges the gap between learning and employability.***

 
 
• The passage identifies a "schism between academic instruction and workplace exigencies" in traditional pedagogy. Skill-based education is described as a "systemic imperative" that "reconciles the persistent dichotomy between **learning and livelihood**."
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: It reduces the duration of education.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage mentions that skill-oriented systems encourage "lifelong learning," but it does not claim that the overall duration of the educational period is shortened.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: It eliminates the need for academic knowledge.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text states that in skill-based education, knowledge is "operationalized" rather than "merely recited," suggesting that knowledge is still used but in a more practical, applied way.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: It focuses solely on manual skills.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage highlights that skill-based education fosters "technological fluency," "communication," and "critical soft skills," which go beyond simple manual labor.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dichotomy**: A division or contrast between two things that are or are represented as being opposed or entirely different. The passage aims to bridge the dichotomy between theory and practice.
 
• **Workplace Exigencies**: The urgent requirements or needs of the modern professional environment.

questions.question: What is the antonym of "Parsimonious"?

• The word **"parsimonious"** means unwilling to spend money or use resources; stingy or frugal. (कंजूस/मितव्ययी)
 
 
• **Example:** The parsimonious man refused to donate even a small amount to the charity.
 
 
• The word **"generous"** refers to someone who is willing to give more of something, especially money or time, than is strictly necessary or expected. (उदार)
 
 
• **Example:** She is known for her generous donations to educational institutions.
 
 
• Hence, the antonym of "parsimonious" is "generous."

• **Example:** She led a frugal lifestyle to save money for her children's education.
 
 
 
• **Economical** (आर्थिक): Using no more of something than is necessary; efficient.
 
 
• **Example:** Buying in bulk is an economical way to save money on groceries.
